statement: For any probability law p on subsets S of [n], with q_i=P(i in S), H_2(p)<=sum_i h_2(q_i). The scalar ratio h_2(q)/q is unbounded as q decreases to zero. Consequently subadditivity alone cannot establish a dimension-free H_2(p)<=C sum_i q_i bound.
assumptions: Finite probability distribution on subsets; base-2 entropy; 0 log 0=0.
source: Independent derivation w505, to be expanded in ATTEMPT.md; not yet a result about all Boolean Fourier spectra.
proof_or_counterexample: Entropy chain rule and conditioning reduces entropy give the bound. h_2(q)>=q log_2(1/q), so h_2(q)/q>=log_2(1/q).
remaining_gap: No gap in the arbitrary-subset-law result; arbitrary laws need not be Boolean spectra, so this is not FEI.

statement: For a Boolean uniform-cube function f(z,y)=g(z)+y h(z), its restriction deficit Delta_y(f)=H_2(f)-(H_2(f_+)+H_2(f_-))/2 equals sum_T r_T[h_2(w_T)+J(t_T)], where a_T=ghat(T), b_T=hhat(T), r_T=a_T^2+b_T^2, w_T=b_T^2/r_T, t_T=2a_T b_T/r_T, and J(t)=1-h_2((1+t)/2). Terms with r_T=0 are zero. In particular Delta_y>=sum_{T:b_T!=0} b_T^2 log_2(r_T/b_T^2)>=0.
assumptions: normalized real Walsh transform under uniform cube measure
source: Independent derivation in ATTEMPT.md, exact local entropy identity.
proof_or_counterexample: Expand phi(a^2)+phi(b^2) using r and w, and phi((a+/-b)^2) using r and t. J>=0 and r h_2(w)>=b^2 log_2(r/b^2).
remaining_gap: No gap in the exact identity under stated assumptions; a universal suitable-coordinate estimate is still unproved.
